message: Radio-link windows from an analytic low-precision ephemeris and the request's link budget. Engineering estimate, not a link guarantee.

model.body_fixed_frame: MOON_ME (mean Earth/polar axis; analytic, optical librations only)
model.time_scale_note: UTC at the API boundary; TT = UTC + 69.184 s (fixed offset, no leap-second kernel); UT1 ~= UTC for the Earth's rotation.

data_provenance.name: Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms (2nd ed., 1998), ch. 12, 22, 47, 53
data_provenance.notes: Truncated ELP-2000/82 series and optical librations. No SPICE kernel, no DEM.

data_provenance.name: Link-budget formulas
data_provenance.notes: Free-space path loss, C/N0, Eb/N0. Hardware figures and ground stations are taken verbatim from the request.

assumptions: ENGINEERING tier: a window means the modelled budget closes with the hardware figures of the request. It is a necessary condition, not a guaranteed radio link.

Ephemeris: analytic truncated series (Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms, ch. 47 and 53), optical librations only. Earth direction from the site is good to ~0.1 deg; near the lunar poles that can shift a window edge by hours. Not cross-checked against SPICE yet.

Lunar side: ideal geometric horizon (elevation 0 deg) on a 1737.4 km sphere; local terrain is ignored. Visibility is tested on the Earth's CENTRE against min_earth_elevation_deg; a ground station can be up to ~0.95 deg away from that direction.

Earth side: a station is usable when the Moon's centre is above its min_elevation_deg (WGS84 geodetic horizon, no refraction, no local mask). Station availability, scheduling and weather are not modelled.

Link budget: free-space path loss only (EIRP + G/T - FSPL - other_losses_db - 10log10(k_B) - 10log10(bit rate)). Pointing, polarisation, atmosphere and lunar-surface multipath must be included in other_losses_db by the caller; none is added here.

Range is station to site (station to Moon centre minus the site's offset along the Earth-Moon line, transverse term <= 4 km). Doppler is one-way, first order in v/c, from a 1 s central difference of that range.

The serving station at each sample is the one with the largest elevation above its own mask. Link windows are the intersection of Earth-visible, any-station-visible and budget-closes intervals; each edge is linearly interpolated between samples, and events shorter than the sampling step may be missed.
Time: UTC at the API boundary; TT = UTC + 69.184 s (fixed, no leap-second table); Earth rotation from Greenwich mean sidereal time with UT1 ~= UTC.
warnings: |latitude| >= 89.0 deg: azimuth is ill-conditioned near the pole. Convention used: local north lies in the meridian plane of the request longitude.
During link windows the Earth is as low as 0.025 deg above the ideal horizon: real terrain can block it and lunar-surface multipath (not modelled) can cause deep fades.
